edges.description: Reduced PHGDH activity decreases de novo L-serine synthesis and can secondarily reduce glycine and D-serine.
Severe biallelic PHGDH dysfunction can produce Neu-Laxova syndrome 1, but the developmental intermediates are unresolved.
Candidate metabolic and signaling consequences may contribute to CNS disease, but their relative causal importance in patients is unresolved.
intermediate_mechanisms: Serine-derived phospholipid synthesis and glycine/D-serine availability.

edges.description: Lower CSF L-serine reports the central biochemical consequence of PHGDH deficiency.
A low or borderline-low fasting value supports the biochemical diagnosis; a nonfasting value is less reliable.
Low glycine can accompany serine deficiency, but normal glycine does not exclude PHGDH deficiency.
Decreased CSF D-serine is a secondary biochemical consequence of reduced serine availability.
Reduced cultured-fibroblast activity functionally reports the enzyme defect.
Decreased plasma phospholipid species report one candidate downstream pathway but do not prove CNS causality.
